summary: A multi-story, cross-shaped institutional building featuring prominent horizontal banding and two tall watchtowers. The structure is surrounded by a dotted perimeter of white blocks. The footprint is a modified cross, with one arm exhibiting an irregular, offset shape.

materials.name: quartz_block
materials.role: horizontal banding, roof trim, and perimeter markers

rebuild_hints: Begin by laying out the cross-shaped footprint, paying close attention to the top-down views to replicate the irregular, zig-zag shape of one of the arms.
Construct the main walls using a repeating pattern of horizontal bands: stone bricks (with windows), wood planks, and white blocks.
Build the two tall towers at the ends of the symmetrical lateral arms using cobblestone, topping them with a flat roof and wooden overhangs.
Cap the main building with a flat roof made of wood planks, bordered by white blocks, and include the small central glass skylight.
Place single white blocks spaced evenly around the structure to form the perimeter boundary.
uncertainties: The exact material of the white blocks is uncertain; it could be quartz, white concrete, or white wool.
The dark stone used for the towers appears to be cobblestone, but could be another dark stone variant.
The interior layout and structure are completely unknown.
